nodes.text: explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Canvas tiering collector (strictly read-only on Canvas): for course 16 "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)" and course 17 "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)", call canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=<literal>, per_page=100, page=1..) following pagination.has_more, always reading the FULL JSON from the output_path file when the preview is truncated. Keep every submission with a user_id. For each graded submission (numeric score AND numeric points_possible) compute the percentage 100*score/points_possible; skip ungraded/nil-score rows. Average per student within each course. Tier by average: "Needs Support" < 60, "Developing" 60-74.99, "Proficient" >= 75. Return ONLY the compact JSON {courses: [{course_id, course_name, tier_counts: {needs_support, developing, proficient}, total_students}], students: [{course_id, user_id, avg_pct, tier}]}. Do not write workspace files or modify Canvas.

explore 1 (financial-market-analyst 0): Market events collector (strictly read-only on the price service): fetch complete daily OHLC histories for GOOGL, AMZN and JPM via the historical-prices tool (interval 1d, enough history such as 6mo, consistent auto_adjust). Find the latest trading date present across the three symbols — the window is the 30 most recent trading days ending on that date, NOT wall-clock based. Compute pct = 100*(Close-Open)/Open per daily row inside the window and take the global top 3 by ABSOLUTE change (deterministic tie-break by date then symbol). Return ONLY the compact JSON {window: {start, end}, events: [{date, symbol, change_pct (2 decimals), description}]} where description states the factual direction and magnitude only (e.g. "GOOGL surged 6.10%", "JPM dropped -3.84%"); do not invent news causes. Do not write workspace files.
